annotations.phase_numbering: the design document's phases: 0 = the Phase 0 skeleton walker (spans, decode chain, accounted regions, gaps), 1 = the Phase 1 parser (header projection, body views, attachment manifest), 2 = routing and statuses, 3 = threading and time evidence
annotations.phase_0_facts: container.*, headers.fields, part.tree, part.regions, part.gaps, body.preamble_epilogue, decode.chain and body.content_sha256 are what the skeleton walker measures today
annotations.phase_1_facts: attach.manifest: the four attachment occurrences with name, declared type, disposition, transfer encoding and content hash (D4's occurrence manifest; routing and statuses stay phase 2)
annotations.labels_are_typed: every value was read out of the fixture bytes with a hex-editor-style line dump and typed by a model from the design rules (D2/D4/D9), never copied out of the walker; labels_provenance is spec because a model wrote them, not a person
annotations.span_conventions: field raw_span covers its line including the line ending; value_span starts immediately after the colon and keeps the leading space; a part's headers_span includes its closing empty line; the CRLF in front of a boundary line belongs to the delimiter region (RFC 2046), so the regions tile the message exactly
annotations.expected_gaps: none decided: every base64 payload decodes and every boundary closes; see labels.undetermined -- the xlsx and png bytes contain octets no strict text rung decodes, so IF the charset ladder is meant to run over binary payloads those two parts would record body.decode_destroyed_bytes, which this label refuses to assert without the design settling the question
annotations.not_yet_labelled: the type verdict triples (declared_mime vs magic vs container_introspection) and routing/statuses for the four attachments (phase 2), quote boundaries (none here), thread edges and TimeEvents (phase 3)
annotations.attachment_bytes: tiny.pdf is 583 bytes with an uncompressed content stream; tiny.xlsx (2268 bytes) and tiny.docx (1284 bytes) are ZIP_STORED zips with pinned timestamps, create_system 0, external_attr 0 and a fixed member order; tiny.png is 82 bytes whose IDAT is stored (uncompressed) deflate blocks -- tests/test_fixtures.py asserts no attachment contains a compressed zip member

value: the design records a decode chain per part (D3) and a deterministic charset ladder (D9, D13) but never says whether the ladder runs over a non-text payload: these four bodies are a PDF, a zip, a zip and a PNG after transfer decoding, so this label gives the transfer verdict (base64) and leaves used_charset and encoding_source null rather than inventing a charset verdict for binary bytes

if the design later says the ladder does run over binary payloads, the xlsx and png bytes contain octets that no strict rung decodes (windows-1252 strict rejects them), so those two parts would record body.decode_destroyed_bytes while the pdf and docx would not -- this label leaves the gap unasserted until that reading is settled, and the question is open in docs/design/label-questions.md
